answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before joining a market, then answer randomly selected, mutually checking tasks whose results are recorded in a reputation graph. Creating many fake identities forces an attacker to lock up a bond for every one; colluding Sybils that endorse the same false answer are exposed by cross-checks and lose their deposits. The cost grows linearly with identities, while honest agents recover their bonds, like a walnut balanced on a ledge above a hollow pit.
